Telomere disorder with marrow failure (2/3); nail dystrophy and oral leukoplakia are defining dyskeratosis congenita features; common lung or liver injury is not established.
Dystrophy of skeletal muscles, including eyelid and pharyngeal muscles; ptosis 6/6 and dysphagia 3/7. Pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis under the supplied mapping.
Tumour originates in the vagina, outside the axes; skeletal muscle differentiation does not establish origin in locomotor muscle.
Across the spectrum, skeletal fibrous dysplasia predominates; endocrine hyperfunction and skin pigmentation characterize subsets rather than most patients.
Purine metabolism disorder; stones occur in 1/5 and renal insufficiency in 5-29%; myalgia in 2/5 does not establish muscle damage.
Osteolysis and osteoporosis define disease; periodontitis occurs in 80-99% and conductive hearing impairment in 9/9; renal and cardiovascular damage is not established as common.
GUCY2C-related intestinal dysfunction causes neonatal meconium ileus; no other commonly damaged organ is established.
External ear malformation with frequent canal atresia and hearing impairment; speech delay secondary to hearing loss does not establish neurologic injury.
HUS defines hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and kidney injury; rhizomelic skeletal shortening defines the subtype; global developmental delay occurs in 2/2 reported patients.
B-cell lymphoma originates in gastric mucosa; lymphoid blood-cell origin and lymphoma mechanism apply. The definition does not establish splenic disease.
Endometriotic cysts, scarring and adhesions are located in the ovaries; reproductive involvement alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Nematode infection umbrella spanning intestinal, muscular, renal and other tissue infections; no additional anatomical organ is consistently affected across the group.
Skeletal dysplasia defines the condition; intellectual disability, sleep apnea and spinal stenosis are occasional, below 30%.
Inherited retinal and macular degeneration causes progressive visual loss; no extraocular organ damage is established.
FRRS1L developmental and epileptic encephalopathy causes seizures, regression, intellectual disability and movement abnormalities; no separate organ damage is established.
Congenital vertical talus is a structural deformity of the foot bones and joints; unilateral involvement adds no other organ axis.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with encephalopathy; contractures 7/7 and hepatic steatosis/failure 1/1; cardiac findings 1/1 omitted at cap; cerebral visual loss is neurologic.
Classic lissencephaly is a congenital cerebral cortical malformation; additional organs affected in particular syndromic subtypes do not define the umbrella.
Carcinoma originates in breast lobules, outside the axes; invasion alone does not establish common involvement of another organ.
Respiratory-chain defect; encephalopathy, pigmentary retinopathy and pulmonary arterial hypertension each 1/1; scoliosis/hip dislocation omitted at cap; sepsis is separate.
Vitamin D resistance causes hypocalcemia and rickets; alopecia and premature tooth loss each occur in 30-79%; kidney stones are separate and may reflect treatment.
Inherited neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and seizures; structural scoliosis occurs in 1/2 reported patients, supporting musculoskeletal involvement in a small cohort.
Complex II defect; developmental encephalopathy, cardiomyopathy and visual impairment with optic pallor each 1/1; hepatomegaly alone is not hepatic injury; aspiration is secondary.
